front: From which aortic cusps do the LMCA and RCA arise?
back: LMCA arises from the LEFT coronary sinus. RCA arises from the RIGHT coronary sinus. No coronary artery arises from the NON-coronary (posterior) sinus.

front: Define coronary dominance and state approximate frequencies.
back: Right-dominant (~80–85%): PDA arises from RCA — supplies inferior wall, posterior 1/3 septum, posterior papillary muscle. Left-dominant (~10%): PDA from LCx. Co-dominant (~5%).

front: Which anomalous coronary course carries the highest SCD risk in young athletes?
back: Interarterial course of an anomalous coronary between the aorta and pulmonary artery (e.g., anomalous LCA from the right sinus, or RCA from the left sinus).

front: Describe ALCAPA and its typical adult presentation.
back: Anomalous origin of the LEFT coronary artery from the PULMONARY ARTERY. In infants: severe HF with ischemia. Untreated adult survivors present with ischemic mitral regurgitation and retrograde flow in dilated coronary collaterals.

front: Define coronary flow reserve (CFR) and its normal value.
back: CFR = peak hyperemic coronary flow velocity / baseline flow velocity (measured by transthoracic Doppler, usually in the distal LAD). Normal > 2.5–3.0. Reduced CFR indicates significant epicardial stenosis or microvascular disease.
